Moderate age-related cerebral abiotrophy was also observed (Figure 1).

report.source_text: At discharge, the patient showed slightly remitted right hemiparesis MRC 4/5; regarding Gerstmann syndrome presentation, no improvements or worsening of the symptoms was observed, and she was prescribed Fludrocortisone for the intracranial hematoma.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Chronic subdural hematoma (Markwalder grade 2, left hemisphere at frontal-parietal level) presenting with atypical Gerstmann syndrome and right-sided hemiparesis in an 86-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a 3-week history of right-sided hemiparesis (MRC 3/5) and complete Gerstmann syndrome manifestations (finger agnosia, agraphia, acalculia, and right-left disorientation). Non-contrast brain CT on admission revealed a chronic subdural hematoma Markwalder grade 2 located on the left hemisphere at the frontal-parietal level, measuring approximately 1.5 cm without mass effect or subfalcine herniation. The left parietal location of the hematoma directly correlated with the clinical presentation of Gerstmann syndrome and the contralateral motor deficit. Follow-up CT on day 2 demonstrated spontaneous resorption with decreased hematoma thickness. The patient was managed conservatively with Fludrocortisone for the intracranial hematoma. At discharge, the right hemiparesis showed slight improvement (MRC 4/5), while the Gerstmann syndrome features remained unchanged.
